notes:
Created 4 cases total in project PR-2005 (379335744), folder __scratch__ (764138): TC-54485 (id 1985019, __mcp-probe-bulkcase-20260921-1), TC-54486 (id 1985020, __mcp-probe-bulkcase-20260921-2), TC-54487 (id 1985021, __mcp-probe-bulkcase-20260921-3), TC-54488 (id 1985022, __mcp-probe-bulkcase-20260921-bad). All four for cleanup. __readonly__ (764093) and TC-54458 (1975349) were never touched.

WRAPPER TRAP -- not encountered, and unambiguous this time. describeCapability explicitly declares test_cases as an UNWRAPPED plain array ('One UNWRAPPED object per case (no per-item test_case key)'), unlike the single-case route where the wrapper turned out to be a real required body field, or create_test_plan_by_integer_id where nesting was rejected. Sent exactly as declared on the first attempt and it worked immediately (200) -- no flat-vs-nested trial needed.

INHERITED FINDINGS FROM create_test_case_by_integer_id, CONFIRMED ON BULK:
1. test_case_steps object-vs-array: same drift, now also present in the RESPONSE contract for this endpoint (declared as a single object with BDD/shared-step-authoring keys; actual is always an array of plain step records). The other declared steps field, test_cases[].steps, is empty on every row despite steps being sent and landing correctly in test_case_steps -- confirmed on both rows of the clean probe.
2. Both duplicate option-id blocks are live on bulk too: row 1 explicitly sent upper-block priority 318618/case_type 318626/status 318632 and got them back unchanged with correct names (Medium/Other/Active). Row 2 sent no option ids at all and defaulted to the LOWER block (priority 318591/case_type 318599/status 318605) -- the project's actual default is the lower block, and the upper block is equally acceptable when supplied explicitly. This matches, and extends, the single-case finding.
3. field_name is declared on case_type/priority/status but present on none, in every row across all 3 invocations; value_category is undeclared and present (always null) on all three objects throughout.

PARTIAL-FAILURE INVESTIGATION -- this was the real point of the probe, and the honest answer is: still open, but what we found is arguably worse than either a clean rollback or a clean partial-commit.

Attempt 2 (200, not a failure -- included in the JSON body above only via this note, not in `attempts[]` since it did not fail): sent one valid row (__mcp-probe-bulkcase-20260921-3, landed as TC-54487/1985021) alongside a row whose test_case_folder_id was set to a nonexistent folder ("999999999"), expecting either a whole-batch rejection or a per-row failure naming the bad row. Neither happened: BOTH rows were created, HTTP 200, success:true. The 'bad' row (TC-54488/1985022) came back with test_case_folder_id "764138" -- the PATH folder -- not the bogus value it was sent with, and its nested `folder` object confirms it actually landed in __scratch__. The invalid per-item value was silently discarded and replaced with the path folder; no error, no warning, no differing status. This directly contradicts the describeCapability guidance text ('test_case_folder_id is required inside each item even though the folder is already in the path... omitting it is the usual cause of a 422 wrapping an upstream 404') -- that text describes what happens when the field is OMITTED; here it was PRESENT but wrong, and the wrong-but-present case degrades silently instead of erroring. This is a real trap: an agent could send a batch intending several rows to land in different folders (or catch a typo'd folder id as a hard failure) and instead have everything silently pooled into the path folder with a fully successful-looking 200.

Attempt 3 (FAILED, recorded verbatim in attempts[]): tried to force a genuine SERVER-side partial-failure by omitting the required `name` field on one row while keeping a valid row alongside it. This never reached the live API at all -- the MCP client itself validates every item in the array against the declared required-field list before dispatch, and rejected the ENTIRE call locally (`{"ok":false,"error":"missing required parameter(s): test_cases.name"}`), blocking the valid row along with the invalid one. No HTTP status was returned because no HTTP request was made.

Net result after 3 attempts: the underlying product question -- does a bulk write half-commit and report 200 when one row is genuinely invalid, and does the response identify which row failed -- remains UNVERIFIED for the missing-required-field class of defect (the MCP client's own schema gate makes that shape unreachable through this tool), and for the one invalid-but-well-typed defect we COULD get to the server (a bad test_case_folder_id), the server did not fail at all -- it silently reinterpreted the row rather than rejecting or partially failing it. Given the max-3-attempt budget, no further attempts were spent. A future probe wanting to test true server-side partial failure would need a defect that is well-typed enough to pass MCP client-side validation but semantically invalid in a way the server does NOT silently paper over (candidates not yet tried: a case_type/priority/status id from neither known block, a folder id belonging to a different project/group, or exceeding the 10-item sync cap combined with a bad row).

COUNT-VS-ROWS: not directly testable on the 200 sync path -- there is no separate top-level `count` field in the 200 response to compare against `data.test_cases.length` (count only appears in the declared 202 async schema). In both successful invocations, data.test_cases.length matched the number of rows sent (2 and 2) with no silent drops or duplicates.

RESPONSE SHAPE: the route returns full created row objects at data.test_cases (not just ids), consistent with the declared 200 schema's structure.

Not exercised in this probe (budget spent on partial-failure instead): unique_id/async 202 path, create_subfolder/scenario_name, attachments/custom_fields first-item-only behavior, the >10-item 400 cap.
